entry.title: WebGPU examples: remove TypeScript type annotations from JavaScript code
entry.content:
Description

Five WebGPU example snippets, taken from the WebGPU Samples (which are written in TypeScript), still have TypeScript type annotations inside js code blocks:

  • function recordRenderPass(passEncoder: GPURenderBundleEncoder | GPURenderPassEncoder) on the GPUDevice.createRenderBundleEncoder(), GPURenderBundle and GPURenderBundleEncoder pages
  • const renderPassDescriptor: GPURenderPassDescriptor = { on the GPUTexture.createView() and GPUTextureView pages

This removes the annotations. For recordRenderPass() I kept the type information as a comment, because the point of that example is that the same function records commands into either kind of encoder.

Motivation

The annotations are syntax errors in JavaScript, so a reader who copies one of these snippets gets a SyntaxError. Prettier also can't parse these blocks, so they are skipped when the Markdown is formatted.

Additional details

I found these by parsing every js code block in files/en-us with Prettier's Babel parser. Apart from blocks that are invalid on purpose (example-bad blocks, the JavaScript error reference pages, and live samples split across several blocks), these five were the only ones that failed to parse. They all parse now. markdownlint, Prettier and the front-matter linter pass on the changed files.

Related issues and pull requests

None that I found.

entry.title: Add an example of arranging items around a circle to cos()
entry.content:
Description

Adds a new example, "Arranging items around a circle", to the Examples section of the cos() page. It places six numbered items in a ring using cos() and sin() with a radius and an item count.

Motivation

Issue #42910 asks for a real-world reason to use cos(). The page's interactive demo already moves a dot around a circle, but it doesn't explain why you would do that. This example shows a practical layout, a radial menu, and explains that each position is calculated from the radius and the number of items instead of being hard-coded.

I put it in the Examples section and left the intro unchanged, because reference page intros should stay a one-sentence summary.

Additional details

The example uses cos(), sin() and the translate property. I checked it in a browser and formatted the file with Prettier using the repo's config. The page build in this PR will show whether it renders correctly in MDN's preview.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42910

entry.title: Add a guide on specifying icons for web extensions
entry.content:
Description

Adds a guide on specifying icons for web extensions: choosing image formats and icon sizes, providing icons for dark mode and in more than one format with icon_variants, and how Safari displays the action icon. Updates the existing icon references to point to the guide, and removes the size guidance they repeated, including Firefox-specific wording that applied to every browser.

Motivation

Icon advice was spread across the icons, action, browser_action and page_action pages and two tutorials, and described Firefox behavior as if it applied to every browser. Safari's handling of the action icon, including the removal of transparent borders, wasn't documented.

Additional details

  • Follows the review on #46363, which this replaces.
  • Specification draft for icon_variants: w3c/webextensions#1134
  • Sizes were read from the Chromium and Firefox sources and from Safari.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #43790

Depends on: #46364

entry.title: Fix EventCounts examples and clarify Event Timing duration thresholds
entry.content:
Description

Fixes the EventCounts loop examples and adds two notes about the duration threshold to the PerformanceEventTiming page.

Motivation

Both EventCounts examples loop with for (entry of ...) without declaring entry, which throws in strict mode and in modules. They now use for (const [type, count] of ...).

The PerformanceEventTiming page didn't say that first-input is reported whatever the threshold, or that buffered entries still use the 104ms default when you set a lower durationThreshold. Both come from the Event Timing spec.

entry.title: [Technical review] Add BiDi bluetooth pages: `disableSimulation`, `handleRequestDevicePrompt`, `simulateAdapter`
entry.content:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the bluetooth module:
    • bluetooth.disableSimulation
    • bluetooth.handleRequestDevicePrompt
    • bluetooth.simulateAdapter
  • Added "Simulated adapter" and "The device prompt" sections to the bluetooth module landing page.

Every example was run against Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server. Firefox doesn't implement the bluetooth module.

Spec links

  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-disableSimulation-command
  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-handlerequestdeviceprompt-command
  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-simulateAdapter-command

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

General

  • bluetooth module spec_url. BCD's webdriver.bidi.bluetooth key points to the Permissions spec (https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/#webdriver-bidi-module-permissions). The module page sets spec-urls: https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-module instead.
  • The bluetooth events. The sheet's Events tab has no bluetooth rows, so BCD has none of the module's four events, though Chrome implements them:
    • bluetooth.requestDevicePromptUpdated
    • bluetooth.gattConnectionAttempted
    • bluetooth.characteristicEventGenerated
    • bluetooth.descriptorEventGenerated

/cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.

Chrome

  • simulateAdapter and disableSimulation. BCD shows both as partial since Chrome 140, with the note "Basic support". In my test run:
    • The simulated adapter applied to every tab, not only to the specified one.
    • simulateAdapter for a tab that already had an adapter also removed its simulated devices.
    • simulateAdapter accepted leSupported for a tab that already had an adapter (spec: invalid argument).
    • Both commands accepted an iframe's context ID (spec: invalid argument).
    • With leSupported: false, getAvailability() still resolved with true (spec: false).
  • handleRequestDevicePrompt. BCD shows full support since Chrome 140, with no note. In my test run:
    • An unknown prompt or device returned unknown error (spec: no such prompt and no such device).
    • An unknown context returned no such frame (spec: no such prompt).
    • A prompt that wasn't handled closed by itself after 0.1 to 2.3 seconds. The spec keeps it open until it's handled.
    • device was accepted with accept: false, which the spec's CDDL doesn't allow.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the compat sheet update.

entry.title: [Technical review] BiDi storage module commands
entry.content:
Description

This PR adds pages for three commands of the storage module:

  • storage.setCookie
  • storage.getCookies
  • storage.deleteCookies

along with corresponding updates to the module overview page and the sidebar.

Question for the @mdn/webdriver team:

The size filter on storage.getCookies and storage.deleteCookies pages: the current description matches the output seen in Firefox 159 and Chrome 156, that is, sum of the cookie’s name and value, in bytes.

The spec describes size as

“byte length of the result of serializing stored cookie as it would be represented in a Cookie header.”

This seems to imply that theme=dark would occupy 10 bytes including the =. However, both browsers return size: 9 and also match a filter with size: 9, which is from counting only theme (5 bytes) and dark (4 bytes), and excluding =.

Should the separator count toward size, or does the spec wording need clarification to reflect the implemented behaviour?

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-setCookie
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-getCookies
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-deleteCookies

Related issues and pull requests

Project tracker: mdn/mdn#851

entry.title: WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial(): editorial review fixes
entry.content:
Firefox 160 adds the required outputLength parameter (matching the spec) in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079306.

This updates the docs with very minor changes to address IDL changes.
The rest of the changes are grammatical suggestions and clarifications from Claude (using the MDN review skill) which I thought were improvements over my grammar:

  • Remove "optional" for the now-required context parameter
  • Correct HMAC-SHA256 key length claim (typical, not required)
  • Fix example intro: it signs an existing token, it doesn't create one
  • Add use case to intro, and split Description into subsections
  • Clarify wording, remove directional language, and use MitM/HTTP/3 consistently
  • Point HMAC link at the HMAC section of SubtleCrypto.sign()
  • Update See also with related reference pages and guide

Related docs work can be tracked in #46281

entry.title: WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream: incoming/outgoingMaxBufferedDatagrams
entry.content:
This adds pages for the incomingMaxBufferedDatagrams and outgoingMaxBufferedDatagrams properties, which replace the non-standard incomingHighWaterMark and outgoingHighWaterMark properties in the specification.

  • The pages are added to the parent interface.
  • This also corrects the old properties and notes the new properties to use. The correction is required because the old pages work in the same way. The spec change was the name, because these properties are not high/low watermarks.
